findings.title: Interpolating queries before the $__range split-eligibility check defeats that check
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on every query *before* `querySupportsSplitting()` is evaluated (line 300), and `querySupportsSplitting()` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` (lines 285-287) to detect the literal `$__range` token and exclude such queries from time-range splitting, because `$__range` is normally resolved to the whole request's range and would be wrong if baked into a split sub-range. Since `$__range` is a Grafana built-in template variable that gets resolved by `templateSrv.replace` (invoked via `applyTemplateVariables`) using `request.scopedVars`, by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable` runs, the literal `$__range` text has already been substituted with the resolved value for the *whole* request range. The detection therefore never matches, so queries using `$__range` are now incorrectly classified as splittable and get partitioned into sub-time-ranges, each sub-query still carrying the stale, whole-range `$__range` value baked in — producing incorrect results for every sub-range chunk. This is exactly the scenario the existing check was designed to prevent.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice: once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside runSplitQuery for every sub-request
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now maps over targets and calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` up front (line 52). The resulting already-interpolated queries are later passed (via `splitQueriesByStreamShard` -> `runSplitQuery`) to `runSplitQuery` in querySplitting.ts, which independently calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` again on every sub-request target (querySplitting.ts line 299). This means interpolation runs redundantly for every shard group/cycle of the same query (confirmed by the updated test expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for what is effectively a single logical query across 4 sharded sub-requests plus the initial call). This wastes CPU cycles on every retry/cycle and risks subtle correctness issues if the interpolation function is not perfectly idempotent (e.g. values containing '$' that could be mistaken for variable syntax on a second pass).

findings.title: No test covers interaction between early interpolation and the $__range split-exclusion check
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only verifies that `$__auto` and `$step` placeholders get replaced before the sub-request is run. It does not add a regression test for a query containing `$__range`, which is the specific case `querySupportsSplitting`/`isQueryWithRangeVariable` is meant to protect (queries with `$__range` should never be split). Because interpolation now happens before that check, such a test would have caught that these queries are no longer correctly excluded from splitting after this change.
